66212.0002.note: Agency fees are 20% of combined Google + Meta spend, per cells B5:M5 of the source workbook. This is not a fixed line: any increase in Google or Meta spend carries a 20% agency surcharge. Every budget ask involving paid media must be priced with it.

unbudgeted_actuals.note: Accounts carrying 2026 actuals with no approved budget line. Every dollar must still appear in the budget-vs-actual table; these become explicit rows rather than being dropped, which is how v1's table under-reported.

targets.definition: Grow 2026 new-customer (M1) NET revenue 19% over 2025 new-customer (M1) NET revenue.
targets.prior_year_basis_note: FY2025 M1 NET on the FROZEN (published) basis. Per Jules 2026-09-04: keep the frozen revenue we are tracking. Closed months use their frozen snapshot values; months not previously published (2026-08 onward) use live figures. The -1.1% drift detected on 2026-09-04 is logged in reports/restatement_2026-08.md and deliberately NOT applied.
targets.caveat: M1 NET revenue is a FLOOR, not total marketing-attributable revenue: any customer whose sales cycle crossed a month boundary contributes zero M1 by construction, and repeat revenue from prior cohorts is excluded entirely. The 2025 cohort alone contributed roughly $1.66M of repeat revenue in Jan-Jul 2026. If leadership's 19% means total revenue growth rather than new-customer revenue growth, this target is materially harder than intended - confirm before publishing.

secondary_frame.name: cohort revenue to date (M1 + repeat)
secondary_frame.why: M1 is the target frame, but it is not what the spend bought. Jan-Aug 2026 cohorts have produced $1,031,222 against $552,656 of M1 - repeat revenue is 46.4% of the total. ROAS on M1 is $4.34; on revenue to date it is $8.09, which already exceeds FY2025's full-year $7.51 at a third of the maturity. Both are reported, always labelled with basis and average maturity.
secondary_frame.maturity_caveat: 2026 cohorts average 4.3 months of maturity against 14.3 for 2025 cohorts. To-date multiples are not comparable across cohorts of different ages: 1.13x at one month, 3.34x at eight.
